title: Multi-dimensional analysis of heat-induced soybean protein hydrolysate gels subjected to ultrasound-assisted pH pretreatment

Multi-dimensional analysis of heat-induced soybean protein hydrolysate gels subjected to ultrasound-assisted pH pretreatment Jinjie Yanga , Jingjing Doua , Bin Zhua , Yijie Ninga , Huan Wanga , Yuyang Huangb , Yang Lia , Baokun Qia,* , Lianzhou Jianga a College of Food Science, Northeast Agricultural University, Harbin, Heilongjiang 150030, China b College of Food Engineering, Harbin University of Commerce, Harbin, Heilongjiang 150030, China A R T I C L E I N F O Keywords: Soybean protein hydrolysate pH Ultrasound Gelation characteristics A B S T R A C T This study aimed to evaluate the gelation characteristics of soybean protein hydrolysate (SPH) extracted by enzyme-assisted aqueous extraction. Specifically, the changes in gelation behaviors for heat-induced (95 ◦ C, 20 min) SPH dispersions treated with pH (pH 3, 5, 9; pH 7 as control) and ultrasound (U; 240 W, 30 min) were investigated. The results showed that typical gel behavior with high elastic nature in the viscoelasticity and network structures were observed during the heating process, where the disulfide bond played a dominant role in the gel network formation of all the samples. Notably, the heat-induced aggregation in the SPH gels was mainly formed by the association of the basic B polypeptide in 11S and β subunit in 7S. The most superior SPH gel was formed at pH 7 when assisted by ultrasonication during the heating process. This as-synthesized gel showed a uniform filamentous structure and exhibited the more excellent textural, rheological and thermal properties than those of the samples formed under acidic and alkaline conditions. These results are of great value in revealing the gelation mechanism of SPH. 1. Introduction Gelation is one of the most crucial approaches to texture food products that can be used to encapsulate bioactive compounds or develop novel food products [1]. Moreover, gels prepared from proteins have great potential in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic sectors. This is because of the renewable, affordable, and biodegradable nature of their building blocks coupled with the large variety of functionalities and physical gelation routes they encompass to form thermal and nonthermal gels [2]. dose.text: Preparation of the SPH gels SPH solution (0.15 g/mL) was prepared by suspending SPH powder in deionized water under magnetic stirring for 2 h at room temperature and stored at 4 ◦ C overnight to enable protein hydration.

endpoint.text: The chemical composition of SPH (61.12% protein, 28.52% carbohydrate, and 10.36% ash) (on a dry weight basis) was measured according to the relevant AOAC methods [18].
Each sample (3 mL) was placed in a 15 mm (diameter) tube, and the spin–spin relaxation time (T2) was measured using a Q-CPMG pulse sequence.
The absorbance of the supernatant was then measured using the BCA method.

reported_results.text: Compared to that of the control, the absolute ζ-potential values of the SPH gels decreased under acidic conditions and increased under alkaline conditions (P < 0.05).
Compared to that of the SPHpH 7 gel, the SH values significantly increased, from 0.07 mmol/g to 0.08, 0.12, and 0.10 mmol/g, for the SPHpH3, SPHpH5, and SPHpH9 gels (P < 0.05), respectively.

In addition, the higher PS observed for the SPHpH 9 gel, compared that of the SPHpH7 gel (P < 0.05), was attributed to the lower aggregation that occurred because of the higher electrostatic repulsion [30].
Different letters (a–e) in the same column indicate significant differences (P < 0.05). 6
Finally, the SPHpH9+U gel formed a higher ordered and more stable structure, as evidenced by the enhanced β-sheet and reduced β-turn structures (P < 0.05).

numbers.text: Preparation of the SPH gels SPH solution (0.15 g/mL) was prepared by suspending SPH powder in deionized water under magnetic stirring for 2 h at room temperature and stored at 4 ◦ C overnight to enable protein hydration.
The chemical composition of SPH (61.12% protein, 28.52% carbohydrate, and 10.36% ash) (on a dry weight basis) was measured according to the relevant AOAC methods [18].
Each sample (3 mL) was placed in a 15 mm (diameter) tube, and the spin–spin relaxation time (T2) was measured using a Q-CPMG pulse sequence.

In addition, the higher PS observed for the SPHpH 9 gel, compared that of the SPHpH7 gel (P < 0.05), was attributed to the lower aggregation that occurred because of the higher electrostatic repulsion [30].
